  "strategy": "alt_strategy",

  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2022,
      "revenue_cr": 14200,
      "net_income_cr": 780,
      "eps": 30.3
    },
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 16500,
      "net_income_cr": 920,
      "eps": 35.8
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 18900,
      "net_income_cr": 1080,
      "eps": 42.0
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Order book of ~INR 19,109 crore as at March 2021 (down from INR 20,503 crore in FY2020) provides 1.5x revenue coverage; management guidance of 50-60% of unsatisfied contract value converting to revenue in FY2022 supports a ~19-20% revenue growth recovery as non-T&D EPC (railway, civil) segments scale up materially after pandemic-related disruptions.",
    "Net profit margin recovers modestly from 5.5% in FY2021 toward 5.7-5.8% by FY2024 as operating leverage kicks in with higher revenues, commodity price risk is partially mitigated via the company's hedging policy, and the high Other EPC (railway/civil) mix \u2014 which grew 53% YoY to INR 4,692 crore in FY2021 \u2014 continues to diversify the revenue base and support margin expansion."
  ],
  "reasoning": "FY2021 is flagged as anomalous: standalone revenue from operations grew only ~13% YoY (INR 11,852 crore vs INR 10,471 crore in FY2020), weaker than the historical trend, reflecting COVID-19 execution delays, though it was partially cushioned by strong railway/civil EPC ramp-up. The 3-5 year CAGR for KEC International has historically been in the 12-16% range. Given the sizeable unexecuted order book of INR 19,109 crore, strong railway segment momentum, and management's guidance that 50-60% of the order book will be executed in FY2022, I apply a recovery-oriented growth rate of approximately 19-20% for FY2022, tapering to ~16% in FY2023 and ~14.5% in FY2024, broadly consistent with the pre-pandemic CAGR adjusted upward for new segment scale. Net income is forecast to grow at a slightly faster pace than revenue as operating leverage and margin normalisation from the pandemic-impacted FY2021 base take hold, with EPS derived on the stable share count of 257,088,370 shares."
}

Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).
